pageCache.pageTitle: Purbrook Park School - Purbrook Park School Parents, Teachers and Friends Association donates over £12,000 of equipment to the Art, Design and Technology department.
pageCache.text:
Purbrook Park School Parents, Teachers and Friends Association donates over £12,000 of equipment to the Art, Design and Technology department.
Purbrook Park School’s hardworking Parents’, Teachers’ and Friends’ Association (PTFA) have donated over £12,000 in funds to the school’s Art, Design and Technology department, including brand new cameras, laptops and storage equipment for pupils.
PTFA Chair, Anna Walsh said “ It has been wonderful to be involved in the fundraising for such vital equipment. All the PTFA are volunteers who give up their time and energy to support the school, and we have organised some really successful fundraising events across the year. We would like to thank the entire school community for helping make these events a success and we hope that you will join us at the Summer Fair on Saturday 4th July.”
Fiona Cumbo, Lead Teacher of the Art, Design and Technology Department was overwhelmed at the donation and said, “We are extremely grateful to the PTFA for the generous purchase of new cameras and laptops. This investment will bring significant value and opportunity to our GCSE pupils”.
Having access to up-to-date equipment enables pupils to develop a wide range of photographic skills, including depth of field, aperture control, and both fast and slow shutter speeds. This broader skill set strengthens their understanding of the technical elements required for success at GCSE level and makes learning more accessible for all pupils studying Photography.
The addition of laptops also provides pupils with greater creative freedom, allowing them to explore Photoshop and other editing tools in more depth, further enhancing their coursework outcomes.
Photography continues to be an extremely popular option, with pupils showing great enthusiasm both in and out of school, often producing exemplary coursework.
Paul Foxley, Headteacher, added, “We are very grateful to everyone who supports our PTFA to raise additional funds to enhance our pupils’ education. This donation will bring new and exciting opportunities for pupils studying Art, Design and Technology at GCSE”.
Purbrook Park School PTFA work hard on fund raising activities throughout the school year and consist of a mixture of parents, staff and friends of the school, who all work towards a common goal – enriching the lives of the pupils who attend the school. The PTFA could not do what they do without every one of their members’ efforts. Thank you Purbrook Park PTFA!
If you would like to get involved with this friendly group of people and help raise funds or donate to the pupils at Purbrook Park School, please contact: purbrookparkptfa@gmail.com.
The PTFA also run a popular Facebook page and invite you to like and follow their page.
https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61552804514154
We invite you to come and join us at the Purbrook Park School Summer Fair on Saturday 4th July from 11.00am until 3.00pm on the school quad. This will feature performances from Purbrook Park School’s talented pupils, craft stalls, cream teas, Pimm’s Tent, children’s games and so much more. Entry is free and everyone is welcome. We hope to see you there!

Personal Development Learning - Tutor Time
On a Monday to Thursday pupils have a 30 minute PDL session with their tutor. During PDL, pupils work in small sized tutor groups with other pupils from their Year group.
Each term during PDL pupils will explore activities around a given theme based on our Character Virtues; 2 per term, different in each year group. The activities are based on Literacy, Creativity, SMSC, The World Around Us and Future You (careers) Tutors will also have the chance to celebrate any tutee successes or special occasions at any point throughout the year.
All year groups take part in a fortnightly House competition within PDL where they will work with the others in their tutor group in the same house to compete against each other.
In years 10 and 11 tutors will also start to focus on sessions based on Work Experience placements (year 10) and College applications, revision skills and literacy across the curriculum to support examinations (year 11).
Raising Standards Leaders deliver fortnightly assemblies to ensure progress, behaviour and standards are maintained within each year group, as well as exploring awareness days and key events throughout the year.
The Character Virtues that we are building to develop and enhance are based on the school motto of Enjoy Enrich Excel;
Tutors know every pupil well, and the tutor group system allows them to mentor and monitor the development of potential in each pupil and helps to promotes equal opportunities for all pupils. It also allows for greater parent partnership, enhanced pupil voice and leadership, and encourages good citizenship.

Tutor time is also used effectively by tutors to support the pastoral care of pupils. Tutor mentoring and tracking along with attendance/behaviour and uniform checks are activities that are embedded each day in our tutor time activities.

pageCache.text:
Purbrook Park Pupils on their way to the National Careers Challenge Final!
This week, Purbrook Park School pupils from years 7 and 8 have been taking part in the National Careers Challenge.
Year 7 were asked to create a sustainable ‘Town of the Future’, sponsored by Air Products. Pupils aimed to achieve net-zero solutions across all aspects of residents’ daily lives, from how to produce goods, to heating homes and travelling to school and work. They had to choose a key employer, consider transport links, house design and food production. They also had to create an advertising campaign to persuade other businesses and residents to relocate to their new town.
Year 8 were asked to create a new subsidiary airline for British Airways that will sit alongside their CityFlyer and EuroFlyer brands. They had to make decisions about who would use their airline, where will it fly to, and how their business will ensure a quality service for their target customers. They had to consider sustainability and how to make it financially viable. They created internal comforts, external marketing, partnership branding, and ideas about staff recruitment and retention.
Kat Millmore-Davies, our Careers Lead, stated, “We saw some fabulous, focused and detailed work across our Year 7 and 8 pupils”.
The visiting presenters leading the day-long workshops were keen to feedback how impressed they were with the original and thorough concepts and ideas produced by our pupils, and that they felt the standard of engagement and behaviour was very high.
We are thrilled to announce that both a Year 7 and Year 8 Team were selected to proceed to the National Finals!
Our Year 7 WINNERS were Oliver, Tommy, Esme, Reuben and Jessica as pictured in the main photo.
Our Year 8 WINNERS were Finley, Daisy, Alex, Charlotte and Isabelle, who are pictured giving their presentation to the judges below.
These pupils will now travel to London on Tuesday 8th July to present their ideas to the celebrity panel, with head judge – Simon Squibb
We are incredibly proud of our pupils at Purbrook Park, and excited to see how they perform on the national stage in July!
Kat Millmore-Davies - Careers Lead

pageCache.text:
Personal Development Learning at Purbrook Park
The intention of personal development is to ensure the holistic development of pupils through exceptional learning opportunities and pastoral care every day. To develop and equip pupils with outstanding character through moral, intellectual, civic and performance virtues, to make a positive contribution to society.
Over-arching purpose and approach;
Our pupils will have enjoyed and immersed themselves in school life through their studies and wider opportunities provided for them. A Purbrook Park pupil can leave our school having gained the confidence and resilience to look after themselves and others. Our pupils will demonstrate knowledge, and respect for, different people’s faiths, feelings and values through diverse learning experiences. Pupils will hold strong moral beliefs for right and wrong and seek out social justice, valuing democracy and the rule of law to make the world a better place for themselves and the wider society. Pupils will acknowledge and embrace their own individuality and celebrate diversity in our school community, taking part in key awareness days activities and events that reflect life in Modern Britain and enrich their school experience. Pupils will be morally proud, intellectually curious, willing to volunteer, demonstrate key leadership skills and know how to build on their own performance in relation to their talents and skills and their own capabilities to excel in their achievements.
At Purbrook Park the Personal Development Framework promotes our key character virtues embedded throughout the curriculum and wider opportunities reflecting our school motto:
Enjoy; ENTHUSIASM FRIENDLINESS MOTIVATION GENEROSITY KINDNESS GRATITUDE CREATIVITY TEAMWORK CURIOSITY AUTHENTICITY
Enrich; INDEPENDENCE INCLUSION VOLUNTEERING CITIZENSHIP UNDERSTANDING INITIATIVE EMPATHY RESPECT COURAGE HONESTY
Excel; SELF DISCIPLINE RESILIENCE DETERMINATION CRITICAL THINKING AMBITION CONFIDENCE EXCELLENCE RESOURCEFULNESS LEADERSHIP JUSTICE
Personal Development Learning is delivered and promoted in the following way;
2 hours of curriculum time per week in tutor groups (4 x 30 minutes sessions Monday-Thursday) focusing on the themes Living In the Wider World, Health and Wellbeing, and Relationships in relation to the Character Virtues https://www.purbrookparkschool.co.uk/page/?title=Personal+Development+Learning+%2D+Tutor+Time&pid=139
1 hour per fortnight of specialist curriculum teaching in PSHE lessons of age appropriate learning in Living In the Wider World, Health and Wellbeing, and Relationships
https://www.purbrookparkschool.co.uk/page/?title=PSHE&pid=715
Cross-Curricular Learning; Science, PE, RS, Food Technology and Computer Science strongly support content addressed in Personal Development Learning. All subject areas have explicit links to SMSC learning and are encouraged to promote the character virtues within lessons.
Fortnightly assemblies will further strengthen the key messages explored in PDL. Year group assemblies provide pupils with career and college information, support transition to secondary school, celebrate pupils’ effort and achievement in all subject areas, raise exam revision profile and support PSHE learning.
After School Enrichment enhance and provide further opportunities for the Character virtues to be developed and explored. RSE, Careers and Basic First Aid Skills are further explored with each year group through our specialist drop down days.
Wider opportunities throughout school life include Children In Need fundraising, Duke of Edinburgh, School Diversity Week, Performing Arts performances, Sports Teams, NCS, Xmas Hamper Appeal, We Are One Expo and many more.

pageCache.pageTitle: Purbrook Park School - Purbrook Park School pupils help Home-Start Havant and Motiv8 Christmas Hamper Appeal 2025
pageCache.text:
Purbrook Park School pupils help Home-Start Havant and Motiv8 Christmas Hamper Appeal 2025
This year, pupils from Purbrook Park School have shown their support for the Home-Start Havant charity (part of Home-Start Hampshire) and to Motiv8, who support local families in need throughout the year. At Christmas, Home-Start run a Christmas Hamper Appeal and the pupils at Purbrook Park School have been instrumental in making this happen!
Becky Smith, Lead Practitioner for Pupil Personal Development said, “I want to pass on a huge thank you to all our pupils, their families and staff who supported our Christmas Hamper appeal once again this year, supporting Home-Start Havant and Motiv8”.
These hampers are really special, with each tutor group being assigned a family to create a special Christmas Day Hamper for them.
We saw a range of delicious Christmas treats, everyday essentials, special Christmas toys and gifts as well as handmade Christmas cards from the tutor groups. The generosity of everyone was once again astounding! The charities were so amazed by each of the hampers.
Janine Milburn, the Havant Team Leader for Motiv8 said “I just wanted to send a huge thank you to all involved in the hampers. The hampers have all been delivered to the families who were met with amazement and tears of joy when they were handed over, and I wanted to want us to pass some of their comments on”.
‘Oh my, I would never have imagined all of this, it is going to be such a massive help’,
‘Amazing, I truly cannot believe this’.
‘I just can’t believe it, thank you, thank you, thank you."
Janine said, “Along with thank you’s and huge smiles from every door we knocked on. I hope your young people realise what a massive difference they have made to the 25 families they donated to. Once again, a massive thank you to everyone who donated”.
Becky Smith, Lead Practitioner for Pupil Personal Development, said, "We are so proud of all the efforts our pupils have made this year and throughout the term exploring Character Virtues that relate to their Year group theme; Year 7 Kindness and Friendliness, Year 8 Enthusiasm and Creativity, Year 9 Authenticity and Teamwork, Year 10 Generosity and Gratitude and Year 11 Curiosity and Motivation. We hope that by taking part in this project our pupils have been inspired to think beyond their own circumstances and consider the impact their actions can have on the wider world”.
If you would like to find out more about the Home Start charity or Motiv8 Havant, please visit their websites below:
https://home-starthampshire.org.uk/ www.motiv8.org.uk
We are pleased to add that this was also published in the Portsmouth News on the link below:
https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/community/purbrook-park-school-pupils-help-home-start-havant-and-motiv8-christmas-hamper-appeal-2025-5451409

Enjoy, Enrich, Excel

SCOPAY - Online Payment system for Parents
SCOPAY
ScoPay is our online payment platform used to pay for school dinners, trips and residentials. It offers convenient mobile access to view balances and manage your account. As part of our cashless system, ScoPay removes the possibility of loss or theft of money from pupils. Parents credit money to their child’s account online via the website with a debit card:
The SCOPAY system can be accessed via a desktop using https://www.scopay.com/login or via the school website: https://www.purbrookparkschool.co.uk/, then clicking on Quicklinks.
It can also be accessed via Edulink, via Links.
How to use SCOPAY on your phone:
Search for "SCOPAY" in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store and download the official app.
Use your existing SCOPAY username and password to log in.
Alternatively, open your phone's web browser (like Chrome or Safari) and go to www.scopay.com.
Once logged in, you can pay for school items, book activities, view payment history, and link multiple children's accounts.
If you haven't set up your account yet, you'll need a unique link code from your school to register.
FAQS
How do I set up my SCOPAY account for the first time?
When a pupil joins the School, their parents/carers are issued with ScoPay login details and a step-by-step activation guide. It is very straightforward to set up an account. Parents/Carers who have more than one child at the school (or a different school who also use ScoPay for online payments) can link their accounts to a single login.
I am being asked for an online link code; what is this?
A link code is a series of letters and numbers that uniquely identifies a child. The code can be used once to link a child to an online account – it cannot be re-used.
A link code can be found on the access letter given to you by your child's school.
I have two children at the same school; can I pay for both of them using one account?
Yes! You can have both children linked to your account by following these steps:
My partner has created an account linked to our child. I tried to create an account with the same link code they used, but it didn't work.
For security, the link code on the letter cannot be used more than once. Please contact your child's school and ask them for a new letter and link code.
I used the wrong email address to sign up. Can I change it?
I know the email address I signed up with.
Log in with the password you specified.
If you have not verified your email address, a message will appear and you will be able to change your email address there.
If you have verified your email address, go to "Your info", and select "Login Details" to change your email address.
I do not know the email address I signed up with.
Please contact your child's school and ask them to unlink your child from the incorrect email address. You can then ask them for a new letter and link code.
Re-register with your intended email address, and use the new link code.
Who should I speak to for help?
If you have forgotten or misplaced your details please contact Mrs Kim Lea, our Data Manager: klea@purbrook.hants.sch.uk who will arrange to resend them to you. For any queries, please call Reception on 02392 370351 or email: admin@purbrook.hants.sch.uk
What cards can I use?
SCOPAY accepts visa debit and Maestro cards
Is it safe to pay online?
Yes. In fact, it is as safe to pay online with ScoPay as it is to use your debit card in a shop or over the phone. ScoPay uses leading technology to process card transactions securely. All communication with the bank is encrypted. Neither ScoPay nor the school have access to your card details and your card details are never kept by ScoPay or the school.
For more information please visit https://www.scopay.com.
Parent Guides
Please click SCOPAY Parent Guides or the advice below for instructions on using your SCOPAY account to its potential.

pageCache.text:
Purbrook Park School Gets Working on National Careers Week
National Careers Weeks was 2nd March – 9th March 2026. Purbrook Park took this opportunity to get all year groups involved in careers activities around the school.
The corridors were enhanced with motivational quotes and career myth busting posters, teachers posted their career paths on their classroom doors, and teachers linked careers to their subject lessons. There were year group workshops throughout the week, and the highlight was speakers who volunteered their time to talk about their career and the path they took to get there.
On Monday, Mr McFawn spoke to Year 10 & 11 pupils about Business Management.
On Tuesday, Dr Qayyum spoke about being a GP and what it was like to work in the medical sector.
Wednesday was the turn of Mr Akhtar, who spoke about the different types of engineering, the options to get there, and where it can take you, both as a career and geographically.
Mrs Aldred talked about floristry, the apprenticeship process to get into the career, where to study and what it was like to make a bouquet for the Queen.
Year 8s completed a career workshop in the main hall with City of Portsmouth College and explored how their personalities can inform their career choices, and their GCSE options.
On Friday Alan Mak MP came to the school to give an assembly about his career path, and what it was like day to day to be a politician. He talked about his education and the importance of self-belief.
Mr Mak MP spoke about the charity work he does, encouraging pupils to get involved in volunteering.
He answered lots of interesting questions, such as, “If you could go back in time, what would you tell your younger self?” and “If you were offered the role of Prime Minister, would you take it?”
Finally, continuing the momentum from Careers week, pupils enjoyed tutor workshops about their future careers and aspirations, supported by Havant & South Downs College.
Sally Akhtar - Careers Advisor

New Year 6 Parents -September 2026
We are delighted to welcome you to Purbrook Park School. We are a thriving and vibrant learning community that strives to achieve the best outcomes possible for the children in our care.
As parents you will want your child to make good progress in a secure and supportive setting. We believe that it is particularly important to ensure that every child has a sense of belonging, experiences high quality learning and teaching, and is offered a curriculum that meets their needs and abilities.
Here at Purbrook Park, we are very proud of our pupils’ success and look forward to welcoming you in September.
Please use the links on the left hand side to find further information about Purbrook Park.
Please review the information below from Skoolkit regarding the uniform and a discount they offer for Purbrook Park pupils.
We will send the following information out to our new Year 7 parents:
Communication
Method
House Allocation Letter
Summer School Information
Uniform Information (attached below)
If you have missed any of the communications above or have any queries about your child starting at Purbrook Park School, please contact the admissions team on admissions@purbrook.hants.sch.uk
